author: Michael Oogwu <198796435+mgkvibez@users.noreply.github.com>
tooling: hand-written, reviewed against the published advisory

statements.impact_statement: The advisory is excessive CPU consumption in dns.name.from_wire_parser(), which is reached only by code that parses DNS wire-format names out of a response. AutoPWN Suite never imports dns, never parses a DNS message body and never validates an email address: name resolution goes through the operating system and the only network client is requests. dnspython is on disk because sigstore depends on pydantic with its email extra, which pulls in email-validator, which declares dnspython. email-validator only reaches the resolver when it is asked to check deliverability, and no path in this product calls it at all, so the vulnerable function is present but unreachable.
statements.status_notes: Reviewed 2026-11-14 against the advisory (GHSA-45c3-73f7-pv4m, fixed in dnspython 2.9.0) and this repository's own lock: sigstore -> pydantic[email] -> email-validator -> dnspython. The earlier note said the email extra is never requested, which is wrong: sigstore asks for it, which is why dnspython appears at all. What matters is that nothing calls it. A search of autopwn_suite/, api.py, autopwn.py and scripts/ finds no import of dns, email_validator or EmailStr, and the update path verifies a Sigstore bundle rather than validating addresses. This statement covers the release that first carries the Sigstore dependency, the one after 2.9.0, so the product is named without a version. The fix cannot be taken yet because dnspython releases containing it require Python >=3.11 and this project supports 3.10. Reassess when that floor moves or when anything here validates addresses.
